points: Q3 2026 will show whether the 2Q26 GMV and revenue momentum — $1.3 billion GMV up 37.9% YoY and $149.7 million revenue up 51.7% YoY — carried through the summer, especially with SezzleCash live and Sezzle Send launching in August.

The print will reveal if active subscriber growth stays near the record 76.4% YoY pace and if MODS growth remains at or above the 31.3% YoY rate from 2Q26; sustained user growth is the core driver of the long case.

Credit quality is the key risk: 2Q26 provision was 2.4% of GMV, and management expects it to build toward the 2.5%-3.0% FY2026 range; Q3 will show if losses are tracking within that seasonal path or threatening the raised $185 million adjusted net income guide.

Operating leverage will be tested in Q3: 2Q26 operating expenses held at 63.3% of revenue and total revenue rose to 11.7% of GMV; the print will show whether that take-rate and cost discipline hold as GMV scales.

The $300 million Mesirow credit facility lowers the cost of capital and funds growth; the Q3 update on utilization and interest expense will shape how much room the company has to invest into the Q4 holiday period.
NDAQ's Oct 22 fintech read-through could set sentiment ahead of SEZL's Nov 6 print; supportive commentary on consumer payments and transaction volumes would reinforce the long setup.

The theme-relative valuation flag already prices SEZL at a PEG discount to fintech peers (0.4x median) and in-line on P/E (1.0x), so the Nov print needs to confirm the 46.5% FY1 EPS growth and the raised $5.25 adjusted EPS guide to keep the rerating alive.
watch: Q3 GMV YoY growth at or above 37.9% — supports the long.
Active subscribers YoY growth at or above 76.4% and MODS YoY growth at or above 31.3% — supports the long.
Provision for credit losses stays within the 2.5%-3.0% FY2026 target range and does not spike above 3.0% of GMV — supports the long.
Management maintains or raises FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $5.25 and adjusted net income of $185 million — supports the long.
